name: Macbeth
blurb: Shakespeare's tragedy of a Scottish general who murders his way to the throne
title: Macbeth Summary: Plot, Characters and Ending Explained
description: Macbeth summary: the witches' prophecies, Duncan's murder, Lady Macbeth's guilt and the fall of Macbeth, act by act, with characters, ending and themes.
h1: Macbeth: Summary, Characters and Ending Explained
answer: Macbeth is a tragedy by William Shakespeare, usually dated to about 1606 and first printed in the 1623 First Folio. It is set in medieval Scotland. After three witches tell the victorious general Macbeth that he will be king, he and his wife are tempted to make the prophecy come true by murder. The play follows what ambition, guilt and fear do to both of them and to Scotland.

head: Character
Who they are

Macbeth's wife, strong-willed and ambitious for him
Supernatural figures, also called the weird sisters, who make prophecies
A general and Macbeth's friend and fellow soldier

The Thane of Fife, a Scottish nobleman

body: Act 1. Scotland has defeated a rebellion and a Norwegian invasion, and the generals Macbeth and Banquo are riding home when three witches greet them. They hail Macbeth as Thane of Glamis, Thane of Cawdor and future king, and tell Banquo that his descendants will be kings though he will not. Moments later, messengers report that King Duncan has given Macbeth the title of Thane of Cawdor, whose holder is to be executed as a traitor. Macbeth begins to think about killing the king. When Duncan names his son Malcolm as heir and announces he will stay the night at Macbeth's castle, Lady Macbeth, who has read her husband's letter about the prophecy, pushes him to murder Duncan and mocks his doubts as cowardice.

Act 2. That night Macbeth sees a vision of a dagger leading him to Duncan's room. He stabs the sleeping king, and Lady Macbeth smears the drugged guards with blood and leaves the daggers beside them. In the morning Macduff discovers the body, and Macbeth kills the guards, claiming rage at their crime. Fearing for their lives, Malcolm flees to England and Donalbain to Ireland, which makes them look guilty. Macbeth is crowned.

Act 3. Remembering that the witches promised the crown to Banquo's line, Macbeth hires murderers to kill Banquo and Fleance. Banquo is killed, but Fleance escapes. At a royal banquet Macbeth sees Banquo's ghost sitting in his place; no one else can see it, and his terrified outbursts alarm the guests. Macduff has refused to attend and goes to England to join Malcolm.

Act 4. Macbeth returns to the witches, who show him apparitions. One warns him to beware Macduff; one says no man born of a woman can harm him; one says he will not be defeated until Birnam Wood comes to Dunsinane Hill. They also show a line of kings descended from Banquo. Feeling safe but angry at Macduff's flight, Macbeth sends men to kill Lady Macduff, her children and her household. In England, Malcolm tests Macduff's loyalty, and the two learn of the slaughter. Macduff vows revenge, and they march on Scotland with English troops.

Act 5. At Dunsinane, a doctor and a gentlewoman watch Lady Macbeth sleepwalk, trying to wash imaginary blood off her hands and speaking about the murders. Malcolm's soldiers each cut a branch from Birnam Wood to hide their numbers, so the forest appears to move toward the castle. Macbeth learns that his wife is dead and reflects that life is meaningless, then goes out to fight.

In the battle Macbeth still trusts that no man born of a woman can harm him, until Macduff tells him he was cut from his mother's womb before birth, a Caesarean delivery. Macbeth realises the witches deceived him with double meanings but refuses to surrender. Macduff kills him offstage and returns with his head. Malcolm is hailed as King of Scotland, promises to reward his supporters and calls Macbeth a butcher and his wife a fiend-like queen, adding that she is thought to have taken her own life.

Each prophecy comes true, but never the way Macbeth expected, and the play leaves open how much the witches caused. One reading is that they only voiced an ambition already inside him, since he thinks of murder at once. Another gives them real power to steer him toward ruin. Lady Macbeth's arc is read as the reverse of her husband's: she begins as the bolder of the two and ends broken by guilt, while he grows harder and more violent. Banquo's line never rules within the play, but the vision of his royal descendants was widely understood as a compliment to King James I, who traced his ancestry to Banquo.

ul: Ambition: Macbeth's desire for the crown, fed by his wife, leads from one murder to many.
Fate and free will: the witches predict the future, but Macbeth chooses every killing, and the play never settles which matters more.
Guilt: blood that cannot be washed off, sleeplessness and ghosts show how the murders destroy both Macbeths from within.
Appearance and reality: the witches' riddles, the hospitable host who kills his guest and Lady Macbeth's advice to look innocent all show that things are not what they seem.
Kingship and tyranny: Duncan and Malcolm are contrasted with Macbeth, whose rule brings fear and suffering to Scotland.
Length: five acts; it is Shakespeare's shortest tragedy and plays in about two hours.
Sources and adaptations: Shakespeare drew on Holinshed's Chronicles; film versions include Akira Kurosawa's Throne of Blood (1957), set in feudal Japan, and Joel Coen's The Tragedy of Macbeth (2021).
Theatre superstition: many actors avoid saying the title inside a theatre and call it the Scottish Play.
Content: murders, including of children, battlefield violence and a suicide.

What teachers usually ask about: who is more to blame, Macbeth, Lady Macbeth or the witches; the dagger and sleepwalking scenes; Macbeth's speech on hearing of his wife's death; and how each prophecy comes true.

check.q: What title does King Duncan give Macbeth right after the witches' prophecy?
check.why: Duncan rewards Macbeth with the traitor's title of Thane of Cawdor, making the first prophecy come true.

check.q: How does Birnam Wood appear to come to Dunsinane?
options: Malcolm's soldiers carry branches cut from the wood
A storm blows the trees toward the castle
The witches move the forest by magic
check.why: The soldiers use the branches to hide how many they are, so the wood seems to move.
Macduff, who was not born in the ordinary way, kills Macbeth in single combat.

faq.q: Why is Macbeth called the Scottish Play?
faq.a: It is a theatre superstition: many actors believe saying the title inside a theatre, except during a performance, brings bad luck, so they call it the Scottish Play.
Her death happens offstage. Macbeth is told only that the queen is dead, and in the last scene Malcolm says she is thought to have killed herself. The play gives no other details.

faq.q: What does "none of woman born" mean in Macbeth?
faq.a: One of the witches' apparitions says no one born of a woman can harm Macbeth, which he takes to mean he cannot be killed. The catch is that Macduff was delivered by Caesarean section, so in the play's terms he was not born in the usual way.
